concepts.name: Right triangle side labels
concepts.summary: Identify the hypotenuse, opposite and adjacent sides relative to a chosen acute angle in a right triangle.

concepts.name: Sine cosine tangent ratios
concepts.summary: Explain sine, cosine and tangent as ratios of side lengths that depend only on the angle, and recall SOH-CAH-TOA.

concepts.name: Reciprocal trig functions
concepts.summary: Recall that cosecant, secant and cotangent are the reciprocals of sine, cosine and tangent respectively.

concepts.name: Degree measure of angles
concepts.summary: Describe angles in degrees as fractions of a full 360° turn and recognise standard angles such as 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°.

concepts.name: Special right triangle ratios
concepts.summary: Understand how the 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles give exact sine, cosine and tangent values for standard angles.

concepts.name: Calculator angle mode
concepts.summary: Understand that a calculator must be in the correct angle mode to evaluate trig functions and read the results sensibly.

misconceptions.text: Sine, cosine and tangent depend on the size of the triangle rather than only on the angle.
The opposite and adjacent sides are fixed features of the triangle regardless of which angle is being used.
Secant is the reciprocal of sine and cosecant is the reciprocal of cosine.

concepts.name: Solving right triangles
concepts.summary: Use trig ratios and the Pythagorean theorem to find all unknown sides and angles of a right triangle.

concepts.name: Angles of elevation and depression
concepts.summary: Model real situations such as heights and distances with right triangles and solve them using trig ratios.

concepts.name: Radian measure
concepts.summary: Define a radian as the angle subtending an arc equal to the radius and convert between radians and degrees.

concepts.name: Unit circle coordinates
concepts.summary: Use the point (cos θ, sin θ) on the unit circle to evaluate trig functions at standard angles.

concepts.name: Reference angles and quadrant signs
concepts.summary: Find trig values of angles beyond 90° using reference angles and the sign of each function in each quadrant.

concepts.name: Inverse trig for angles
concepts.summary: Apply inverse sine, cosine and tangent to find an acute angle from a known ratio.

concepts.name: Pythagorean identity basics
concepts.summary: Use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to find one function value from another given the quadrant.

misconceptions.text: Radians and degrees are different kinds of quantities, so a radian value cannot be compared with a degree value.
Trig functions of angles larger than 90° are undefined because there is no right triangle.
sin⁻¹(x) is the reciprocal 1/sin(x), rather than the inverse function that returns the angle whose sine is x.

concepts.name: Law of sines
concepts.summary: Apply a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C to find missing sides or angles in non-right triangles.

concepts.name: Law of cosines
concepts.summary: Apply c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C to triangles given SAS or SSS information.

concepts.name: Ambiguous SSA case
concepts.summary: Analyse SSA data to decide whether it yields zero, one or two triangles.

concepts.name: Graphs of sine and cosine
concepts.summary: Sketch y = sin x and y = cos x and read zeros, maxima, minima and periodicity from them.

concepts.name: Amplitude period and phase shift
concepts.summary: Analyse how A, B, C and D transform a sinusoid and write an equation from a graph.

concepts.name: Angle-sum and difference identities
concepts.summary: Apply the sum and difference formulas for sine, cosine and tangent to evaluate exact values and simplify expressions.

concepts.name: Basic trig equations
concepts.summary: Solve equations like 2sin x = 1 over a given interval by finding all solutions using symmetry and periodicity.

concepts.name: Domain and range of inverses
concepts.summary: Analyse why inverse trig functions need restricted domains and state their principal value ranges.

misconceptions.text: The law of sines can be used with any three given pieces of a triangle.
sin(A+B) equals sin A + sin B.
In y = sin(Bx − C), the phase shift is C rather than C/B.

concepts.name: Double and half-angle identities
concepts.summary: Derive double and half-angle formulas from the sum identities and choose among cos 2θ forms strategically.

concepts.name: Proving trig identities
concepts.summary: Analyse both sides of an identity and select substitutions such as Pythagorean, reciprocal and quotient forms to prove it rigorously.

concepts.name: Product-to-sum and sum-to-product
concepts.summary: Use product-to-sum and sum-to-product identities to transform expressions for simplification or solving.

concepts.name: Complex trig equations
concepts.summary: Solve equations needing factoring, quadratic substitution, multiple angles or identities, and check for extraneous solutions.

concepts.name: Harmonic form conversion
aliases: a sin x + b cos x
concepts.summary: Rewrite a sin x + b cos x as a single sinusoid and judge when this form simplifies a problem.

concepts.name: Graphs of other trig functions
concepts.summary: Analyse the graphs of tangent, cotangent, secant and cosecant, including asymptotes, periods and links to sine and cosine.

concepts.name: Sinusoidal modelling
concepts.summary: Fit and evaluate sinusoidal models for periodic data and judge their validity and limitations.

misconceptions.text: To prove an identity you may apply operations to both sides, such as cross-multiplying, as with solving an equation.
Squaring both sides or dividing by a trig factor is always safe when solving trig equations.
cos 2θ has only one correct form, 2cos²θ − 1.

concepts.name: Euler's formula connection
aliases: e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ
concepts.summary: Evaluate how Euler's formula unifies trig identities and derives angle-sum results.

concepts.name: De Moivre's theorem applications
concepts.summary: Use de Moivre's theorem to derive multiple-angle formulas and roots of unity, judging when it beats real identities.

concepts.name: Trig substitution strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate when substituting sin, tan or sec simplifies radicals and constraints, and justify the chosen domain.

concepts.name: Small-angle approximation analysis
concepts.summary: Assess the accuracy and error of approximations such as sin x ≈ x and cos x ≈ 1 − x²/2.

concepts.name: Fourier series intuition
concepts.summary: Judge how periodic functions can be built from sums of sinusoids of different frequencies, and what amplitude and phase represent.

concepts.name: Designing trig-based models
concepts.summary: Design and justify trigonometric models or solution methods for novel problems in surveying, navigation or oscillation.

concepts.name: Constructing original identity proofs
concepts.summary: Create new proofs of identities and laws, such as the law of cosines from coordinates or sum formulas from geometry.

misconceptions.text: The small-angle approximation sin x ≈ x holds for angles in degrees as well as radians.
A trig substitution works over any domain without needing to check the sign of the resulting root.
Euler's formula is just a notational convenience and gives no new way to derive trig identities.
